cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. That ink on your new sofa must be from the delivery label.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The label's dry. You signed with your fountain pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Then the driver brushed my signature against the fabric. We should photograph it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pen's still leaking onto the cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The delivery must have cracked it when they squeezed past me. Photograph the pen too; that's a second claim.

mechanism: A uses apparently expert evidence-handling corrections to reassign each ink clue to delivery damage rather than A's pen use.
confusable: Simple denial would repeat innocence; D133 must actively redirect each new clue toward a safer cause.
comparison: Consumer-delivery claim differs from an installer reclassifying their own shelf markings.
seedUse: Keep wet signature, leaking pen and delivery hypothesis; make A correct how B tests and records evidence.
